'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark]]
****[[Prime Minister of Denmark|Prime Minister]] [[Mette Frederiksen]] announces the increase of the COVID-19 risk level from level 4 to 5, indicating "widespread infection in society", as well as "a risk that treatment capacity at hospitals will be exceeded". In addition, public and private gatherings will be limited to five people. The rules will be in effect until January 17. [https://www.thelocal.dk/20210105/latest-denmark-moves-to-highest-covid-19-alert-level-amid-concerns-over-b117-variant (''The Local Denmark'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****[[Chancellor of Germany|Chancellor]] [[Angela Merkel]] and leaders of 16 [[States of Germany|states]] agree to extend the country's [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] until January 31. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/01/05/coronavirus-germany-poised-to-extend-nationwide-lockdown-amid-high-infections-and-deaths (Euronews)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****[[Italy]]'s [[Council of Ministers (Italy)|Council of Ministers]] approves a decree that prohibits travel between the country's regions except for health or work reasons, with people in "red zone" areas only allowed to move once per day. They also extend most [[COVID-19 lockdown in Italy|lockdown]] restrictions until January 15. The country will be in a "yellow zone" on January 7 and 8, with eased restrictions and allowing restaurants, bars, shops and malls to open, while on January 9 and 10 the country will be in an "orange zone", with malls closed and restaurants and bars open for takeaway and delivery only. [https://www.ansa.it/sito/notizie/politica/2021/01/05/covid-le-misure_2b945e85-3ac6-4820-a8a7-f04f22a0b1b3.html (ANSA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malta]]
****[[President of Malta|Maltese president]] [[George Vella]] receives his first dose of the COVID-19 vaccine. [https://timesofmalta.com/articles/view/president-george-vella-to-get-covid-19-vaccine-live-on-air.842961 (''Times of Malta'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Northern Ireland]]
*****The [[Northern Ireland Executive]] issues a [[stay-at-home]] order in [[Northern Ireland]], which is currently in the second week of a six-week lockdown, legally enforceable from January 8, in order to reduce the spread of COVID-19. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-northern-ireland-55538236 (BBC News)]
****The [[United Kingdom]] reports a record 60,916 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2,774,479. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/health/uk-covid-cases-today-death-toll-b1782686.html (''The Independent'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Ministry of Health (Indonesia)|Health Minister]] Budi Gunadi Sadikin announces that a nationwide mass [[vaccination]] program against [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] will begin on January 13. [[President of Indonesia|President]] [[Joko Widodo]] will become the first person in the [[Indonesia|country]] to receive a [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://kontan.co.id/news/indonesia-says-mass-vaccinations-to-begin-january-13-president-to-get-first-shot (''Kontan'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]], [[Variant of Concern 202012/01]]
****[[Iran]] reports its first case of a new variant of [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS-CoV-2]] in an [[Iranian peoples|Iranian]] who travelled from the [[United Kingdom]] and later tested positive for COVID-19. [https://www.jpost.com/breaking-news/iran-finds-first-case-of-new-virus-variant-in-traveler-from-uk-654329 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]]
****The [[Israel|Israeli]] [[Cabinet of Israel|Cabinet]] agrees to tighten the nationwide lockdown by closing schools and non-essential shops for 14 days. The measures will come into force at midnight between Thursday and Friday. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/ministers-approve-2-week-full-lockdown-to-counter-mushrooming-virus-cases/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Japan]] reports a record 4,915 new cases in the past 24 hours. In addition, a record 76 deaths are also reported in the past 24 hours. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2021/01/05/national/tokyo-coronavirus-over-1200/ (''The Japan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oman]], [[Variant of Concern 202012/01]]
****[[Oman]] reports their first case of a new variant of [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS-CoV-2]] in a resident who travelled from the [[United Kingdom]] and tested positive while in quarantine. [https://www.khaleejtimes.com/coronavirus-pandemic/new-covid-variant-oman-registers-first-case-in-uk-traveller (''Khaleej Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[South Korea]] surpasses 1,000 deaths from COVID-19. [http://www.koreaherald.com/view.php?ud=20210105001029 (''The Korea Herald'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Rwanda]]
****[[Rwanda]] bans public and private transport in and out of [[Kigali]] and between districts and extends a curfew from 8:00 p.m. to 4:00 a.m. local time for another 15 days amid a deadly second wave of COVID-19. [https://www.monitor.co.ug/uganda/news/rwanda-restricts-movement-as-coronavirus-cases-surge-3247948?view=htmlamp (''Daily Monitor'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Zimbabwe]]
****[[Zimbabwe]] reports 1,365 new confirmed cases and 34 deaths in the past 24 hours, its largest daily increase for both cases and deaths since the pandemic began as the country begins a month-long lockdown to reduce the spread of COVID-19. [https://www.reuters.com/article/healthNews/idUSKBN29A2HM?il=0 (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Georgia (U.S. state)|COVID-19 pandemic in Georgia]], [[Variant of Concern 202012/01]]
****[[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]] reports their first case of a new variant of [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS-CoV-2]] in an 18-year-old male with no travel history, and who is currently in isolation at home. [https://www.11alive.com/article/news/health/coronavirus/first-case-of-covid-19-variant-identified-in-georgia/85-ca54420c-9086-4dc5-a1c8-bfa18dde31ea (WXIA-TV)]
***The U.S. surpasses 21 million cases of COVID-19, just four days after surpassing 20 million cases. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/01/05/health/us-coronavirus-tuesday/index.html (CNN)]
 
'''International relations'''
*[[Qatar diplomatic crisis]]
**[[Saudi Arabia]] reopens its border with [[Qatar]], ending the three-year diplomatic crisis. The resolution was brokered by [[Kuwait]] and the [[United States]]. ([https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/saudi-arabia-lifts-blockade-qatar-breakthrough-agreement-eases-gulf-crisis-n1250102 NBC News])
*[[Kosovo–United States relations]]
**[[Kosovo]]'s [[Assembly of the Republic of Kosovo|parliament]] unanimously approves deploying the [[Kosovo Security Force]] on international [[peacekeeping]] missions, following a formal request by the [[United States Central Command]]. [https://www.timesunion.com/news/article/Kosovo-approves-sending-army-troops-on-15848194.php (''Times Union'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2020–2021 United States racial unrest]]
**[[Shooting of Jacob Blake]], [[Kenosha unrest]]
***[[Kenosha unrest shooting]]
****Kyle Rittenhouse, the 17-year-old boy accused of shooting three people (including two killed) during a protest in [[Kenosha, Wisconsin]], will plead not guilty. [https://www.newsweek.com/kyle-rittenhouse-pleads-not-guilty-shooting-3-people-kenosha-prepares-protests-1559123 (''Newsweek'')]
***[[Kenosha County, Wisconsin|Kenosha County]] District Attorney Michael Graveley announces that no charges will be made against Rusten Sheskey, the Kenosha police officer accused of shooting Jacob Blake. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2021/01/05/kenosha-officer-rusten-sheskey-not-charged-jacob-blake-shooting/6554345002/ (''USA Today'')]
*[[2020 United States election protests]]
**[[List of mayors of Washington, D.C.|Washington, D.C. mayor]] [[Muriel Bowser]] activates the [[District of Columbia National Guard]] due to an organized protest of pro-Trump supporters. [https://apnews.com/article/joe-biden-donald-trump-politics-electoral-college-muriel-bowser-1634bf71a27de48efef3cd1e6ed4abe4 (AP)]
**A federal judge bans [[Proud Boys]] chairman [[Enrique Tarrio]] from entering [[Washington, D.C.]] [https://www.forbes.com/sites/jemimamcevoy/2021/01/05/proud-boys-leader-released-from-jail-banned-from-wednesday-protests-in-dc/?sh=5cdcba8e6c62 (''Forbes'')]
*[[Iran–United States relations]]
**[[Iran]] requests that [[Interpol]] issue a [[red notice]] for the arrest of [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] and 47 other U.S. officials for their role in the [[assassination of Qasem Soleimani]] in January 2020. A similar request was previously rejected by Interpol. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/1/5/iran-issues-interpol-notice-for-48-us-officials-including-trump (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Censorship in Vietnam]]
**A court in [[Vietnam]] [[sentence (law)|sentences]] three [[freelance journalist]]s to between 11 and 15 years in prison for anti-state [[propaganda]], criticising the [[government of Vietnam|government]] and "infringing the interests of the [[Communist Party of Vietnam|Communist Party]]", among other [[criminal conviction|convictions]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-vietnam-security-trial/vietnam-jails-journalists-for-propaganda-critical-of-state-idUSKBN29A0VI (Reuters)]
*[[Trump–Raffensperger phone call]]
**[[Cleta Mitchell]] resigns from her law firm after participating in President Trump's phone call with [[Georgia Secretary of State]] [[Brad Raffensperger]]. [https://thehill.com/homenews/administration/532789-attorney-on-trump-call-with-georgia-secretary-of-state-resigns-from (''The Hill'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2020 United States Senate elections]]
**[[2020–21 United States Senate election in Georgia]], [[2020–21 United States Senate special election in Georgia]]
***Voters in [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]] head to the polls to cast their votes to determine who will control the [[United States Senate]]. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] Senator [[David Perdue]] will face [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrat]] [[Jon Ossoff]], and incumbent Republican [[Kelly Loeffler]] will face Democrat [[Raphael Warnock]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/election-us-2020-55489392 (BBC News)]

'''Sports'''
*[[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama]] [[wide receiver]] [[DeVonta Smith]] wins the [[Heisman Trophy]], making him the first receiver to do so since [[Desmond Howard]] in 1991. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/alabama-crimson-tide-wide-receiver-devonta-smith-wins-heisman-trophy-2021-01-05/ (CBS News)]
*[[United States men's national junior ice hockey team|Team USA]] defeats [[Canada men's national junior ice hockey team|Team Canada]] 2–0 in the gold medal game to win the [[2021 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships]], while [[Finland men's national junior ice hockey team|Team Finland]] defeats [[Russia men's national junior ice hockey team|Team Russia]] 4–1 in the bronze medal game. Team USA's [[Trevor Zegras]] is named MVP of the tournament. [https://www.cbc.ca/sports/hockey/canada-us-world-junior-final-recap-1.5862647 (CBC News)]
